items.title: Why diverting maize for ethanol is affecting poultry farmers
items.summary: Despite a record maize production last year, India’s poultry farmers are contending with higher retail prices of the poultry staple due to its increasing demand for ethanol blending. With a decline in sowing and deficient rainfall this year, experts say this is likely to get worse. Maize was available to poultry farmers for Rs 12-14 per kg around the year 2019 but it now sells for Rs 27-28 per kg in the retail market. Since maize is the primary, starch-heavy food for all poultry and soymeal is the secondary food, farmers maintaining egg-layer and broiler poultry are both facing a crisis. They have to buy feed at these high prices and either pass on the cost to the consumer or bear the losses. The contribution of maize towards ethanol blending increased from 0% in 2021-22 to around 37% in 2025-26. India’s move to blend 20% ethanol in petrol has been a subject of much discussion this past year after vehicle owners alleged damage due to the biofuel. Besides, when sugar prices surged recently, it led to debate on whether it was due to the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme. Poultry farmers from Maharashtra spoke to ISignal of their losses, especially when a weak monsoon might mean lower maize and soybean production this year, and said that unless maize cultivation increases, it should not be diverted for ethanol. Eggs are a cheap source of protein , important to improve the nutritional status of Indians. The E20 programme is targeted at reducing India’s import bill from fossil fuels such as petrol and diesel. But if the area under maize cultivation goes up at the expense of pulses and oilseeds and we have to import them, would that not cancel the E20 gains and therefore miss the point, asked agriculture expert R. Ramakumar, a faculty member at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, currently on sabbatical. ISignal wrote to the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairy for comment on how the government plans to protect the interests of poultry farmers in this context. We will update this report when we receive a response. items.title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules 2026: From consumer disclosure to platform governance
items.summary: On September 9, 2026, the Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India, notified the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (the “ Amending Rules ”), amending the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020. The Amending Rules will come into force on January 1, 2027. The E-Commerce Rules apply broadly to e-commerce entities, covering both marketplace and inventory models, as well as e-commerce retail activities and unfair trade practices across e-commerce models. They also extend to entities established outside India where they systematically offer goods or services to consumers in India. Read together with the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the Amending Rules mark a shift in regulatory focus from disclosures addressed to the consumer, to more direct regulation of how e-commerce platforms are built, operated and presented to users. The changes affect search and ranking, sponsored listings, discount pricing, seller and marketplace disclosures, invoicing, dark patterns, and the use of consumer information. Ranking and search Amended Rule 3(1)(j) widens the definition of “ranking” to cover the prominence given not only to goods and services but to sellers themselves, irrespective of the technology used to present or organise them. Further, new Rule 4(11)(c) separately prohibits manipulating search results or indexes in a manner that misleads users having regard to their search query, and Rule 4(12) requires sponsored listings to be clearly and prominently identified as such. Rule 5(3)(f) correspondingly requires marketplace entities to explain, in descending order and in plain, intelligible language, the parameters that principally determine ranking, together with their relative weight. Notably, this requirement is limited to explaining the factors that drive visibility, rather than requiring disclosure of an algorithm or source code. Takeaway: E-commerce entities will need to ensure greater transparency in how products and sellers are ranked and displayed, including by clearly identifying sponsored listings and explaining the principal parameters that determine ranking. The objective is to enable consumers to distinguish between organic search results and commercially influenced placements. items.title: Why are voter IDs mandatory for benefits under CM's scheme for women? P&H High Court asks Punjab
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently asked the Punjab government to clarify the purpose behind making voter identity card mandatory for grant of benefits under the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, a financial assistance scheme to provide monthly income support to women [Harbakhsh Charitable Society v State of Punjab & Others] A Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor sought the clarification on September 24 after hearing a plea challenging the scheme on the ground that it sole purpose is to secure votes in favour of the Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab. It was argued that the mandatory requirement of the voter ID card of Punjab State for getting the scheme benefits clearly indicates that its object is only to secure votes from the beneficiaries. While adjourning the matter to October 5, the Court said, "Learned Additional Advocate General, Punjab opposes the petitioner’s claim and seeks adjournment in order to obtain instructions and clarify the purpose for which Voter ID card is made mandatory for grant of benefit under the Scheme." Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor While eligible women from the general category receive ₹1,000 per month under the scheme, those belonging to Scheduled Castes receive ₹1,500 monthly. The scheme has been challenged by way of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Harbakhsh Charitable Society. It has argued that while Voter ID card can be one of the documents required for the purposes of identification, requiring it mandatorily for the grant of benefit under the scheme manifests its purpose, that is to act as a quid pro quo for securing votes. The PIL states that Punjab government repeatedly pleads financial constraints before the Court when asked to discharge its admitted statutory liabilities towards its employees and pensioners but yet, it continues to incur substantial recurring expenditure upon discretionary subsidy or freebie schemes. "The said approach, according to the Petitioner, reflects an arbitrary and irrational prioritisation of public resources and raises issues concerning fiscal accountability, good governance and the constitutional obligation to utilise public funds in a reasonable and non-arbitrary manner," the plea said. items.title: Law Student moves Supreme Court alleging UP govt misled court, no action taken against Executive Magistrate who issued notice over CJP protest
items.summary: Law student Akshat Tripathi has moved the Supreme Court alleging that the Uttar Pradesh government misled the court on the action taken over the ₹5 lakh bond notice issued to him in connection with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest. Tripathi had initially filed a petition before the Court over the notice. His petition was mentioned on September 10 before a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana , which is hearing petitions arising out of the July protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. On that day, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, on instructions from the State of UP, had told the Court that the notice was issued not by the District Magistrate but by the Executive Magistrate, and that the official responsible has been suspended. "It was not the District Magistrate. It was some other official who has been suspended. Let's not sensationalise it," Mehta had said. In his fresh application, Tripathi has relied on an Indian Express report to state that UP DGP Headquarters later clarified that only Sub-Inspector Shiva Pandey, whose report formed the basis of the notice, was suspended. The ACP (Executive Magistrate) who actually issued the notice was not. "It is pertinent to mention that the State of Uttar Pradesh misled this Hon'ble Court by placing a wrong statement regarding the action taken by the State authorities and that too by using the good office of the learned Solicitor General of India," the application states. By way of background, a notice dated September 4 was issued under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) by the Executive Magistrate-Third, Greater Noida. It called upon Tripathi to show cause why he should not be bound under with a personal bond of ₹5 lakh and two sureties of like amount, for allegedly instigating fellow students to join a proposed CJP dharna. The notice came three days after the Supreme Court's September 1 order quashing cases against students who took part in the CJP-led protests against exam paper leaks. items.title: TN cop clings to SUV roof for 30 km to stop gutka smugglers in Coimbatore
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. For nearly 30 km, a head constable clung to the roof rails of a speeding SUV as police chased its occupants, who were allegedly trying to flee with around 170 kg of gutka and other banned tobacco products in Coimbatore on Sunday, September 27. The chase ended near Thekkalur on the Tiruppur district border, where police arrested three men and seized the contraband. The incident began around 5.45 am when a team from Kovilpalayam police station, led by Sub Inspector V Vignesh and Head Constable M Velmurugan, was checking vehicles between Vilankurichi and Kalappati. The officers attempted to stop a Karnataka-registered SUV suspected to be carrying gutka. According to the police, the occupants initially refused to stop but slowed down later. When the officers noticed bundles inside the vehicle, Vignesh attempted to search it. The occupants allegedly pushed the policemen, shut the doors, and accelerated towards Avinashi. Velmurugan reportedly told The New Indian Express that the driver suddenly accelerated while the police were trying to stop the vehicle, trapping his hand in the door. Fearing that the suspects would escape, he grabbed the roof rails and pulled himself onto the top of the SUV. The SUV continued at high speed through Vilankurichi, Kalappatti Four Roads, and Coimbatore Airport Junction, heading towards Kaniyur Toll Plaza. Velmurugan remained on the roof as the occupants allegedly attempted to evade the police. The SUV crossed the toll plaza through the emergency lane and continued towards Avinashi. Police personnel in another vehicle followed the SUV, while information about the chase was passed to Karumathampatti police and Highway patrol teams on Avinashi Road. They, along with ambulance drivers and volunteers from the surrounding areas, joined the chase. Avinashi police were also alerted and began looking for the vehicle. Motorists who saw the constable clinging to the roof recorded videos of the incident. The clips were later circulated on social media. The pursuit ended near Thekkalur, close to the Tiruppur district border, after police and ambulance vehicles surrounded the SUV and the occupants gave up. Two of the men attempted to flee but were caught by Avinashi police shortly afterwards. They suffered fractures to their arms while attempting to flee, police said. items.title: Telangana’s school education crisis: Citizens’ group seeks fee cap, more public schools
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Uncapped, exorbitant fees in Telangana’s private schools and a weakening public education system are two sides of the same coin, the Telangana People’s Front said, demanding action from the state government on both issues. The organisation, comprising former bureaucrats, academics, and activists, held a public meeting on the state of school education in Telangana in Jawaharnagar, a suburb of Hyderabad, on September 27. Concluding a two-week ‘vidya bus yatra’, during which its members visited government schools across Telangana, the organisation put forth three demands for legislative changes: pass the long-pending private school fee regulation Bill , bring in a law mandating Telangana Public Schools in every mandal to strengthen public schools, and also a legal mandate to allot 18% of the state’s annual budget for education. The people of Jawaharnagar reiterated their demand for an integrated school for Classes 1 to 12 in Gabbilalpet, citing the lack of adequate schools in the area. Jawaharnagar, which houses Hyderabad’s main dumpyard, is home to many migrant workers, mainly from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, and Backward Class communities. Residents have been leading a campaign for a school that was sanctioned by the education authorities in Medchal-Malkajgiri district. However, the land allotted for the school remains under litigation, leaving many children unable to attend school. Kavya, a first-generation learner from Jawaharnagar who is now pursuing graduation, said that while she managed to complete her schooling from a local government high school, the children of her neighbourhood deserve better schools and a better future. “They must not grow up feeling like second-class citizens,” she said. The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against former Tamil Nadu minister and Tiruvannamalai MLA EV Velu, his son EV Kumaran, and several government officials, contractors and private individuals over the alleged illegal excavation of lake-bed material in Tiruvannamalai district to level land for a Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) conference held in December 2025. The FIR was registered on September 24, based on a complaint filed by Jayaram Venkatesan, convenor of the anti-corruption organisation Arappor Iyakkam, with the DVAC director on August 14. According to the FIR, the alleged excavation took place at Malappambadi Lake between November and the first week of December 2025, ahead of the DMK northern zone youth wing conference held on December 14 at Kalaignar Thidal in Malappambadi. The conference venue was spread across around 124.56 acres owned by Kumaran, the FIR said. Kumaran is a director of Arunai Products and Services Pvt Ltd, which purchased the property from Rishi Enterprises for Rs 46 crore on June 12, 2024. At the time, Velu was the Minister for Highways, Minor Ports and Public Works, as well as the DMK’s northern zonal in-charge and Tiruvannamalai (south) district secretary. The FIR alleged that he misused his official position and facilitated the excavation and transportation of lake-bed material to the conference site to level the land. The complaint alleged that around 45,72,058 cubic feet of lake-bed material was removed from Malappambadi Lake, causing an estimated loss of Rs 8.22 crore to the government exchequer. According to the FIR, Malappambadi Lake, which covers around 70.65 acres, was not among the waterbodies included in a June 19, 2024 notification issued by the district administration permitting the removal of clay, silt and gravel. The DVAC said Kumaran had not obtained permission from the Revenue Department, Corporation or Geology and Mining Department to remove gravel or other lake-bed material from Malappambadi Lake.
